say.text: A baby is brought to the clinic with bluish lips, and the examining doctor suspects congenital heart disease.
Of the cyanotic congenital heart diseases, which is the most common?

choices.label: Not sure, give me a hint

say.text: Look for the lesion whose severity of presentation tracks how tight the right ventricular outflow is.
A blue newborn makes other names tempting, and only one lesion tops the cyanotic list. This one is not it.
Think again about which condition is described by right ventricular outflow obstruction.

sure_note.text: You felt sure, so this is worth a second look: the name that heads the cyanotic list is tied to how tight the right ventricular outflow is.

say.text: Same baby. Which is the most common cyanotic congenital heart disease?
It is Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF), the most common cyanotic congenital heart disease, and its presentation varies with how severe the RVOT obstruction is.
The other names are cyanotic too, which is why they tempt, but they do not hold this title. We will return to it shortly.
Yes. TOF is the most common cyanotic congenital heart disease, and how it presents varies with the severity of right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) obstruction.
The same baby is diagnosed with TOF. A classic NEET PG stem follows.
Which is NOT one of the four components of classic TOF?

choices.label: Not sure, give me a hint

say.text: Four components, built around one large defect in the ventricular septum. Ask which options fit that picture and which sit elsewhere in the heart.
It sounds like a complication, so it is easy to treat as an extra. But the overriding aorta is one of the four classic components.
Look for a defect that sits outside the four.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so check the list again: the four are a VSD, an overriding aorta, infundibular RVOT obstruction and right ventricular hypertrophy.

say.text: Hypertrophy sounds like a result rather than a defect, so it is tempting to drop it. But right ventricular hypertrophy is the fourth classic component.
Look for a defect that sits outside the four.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so check the list again: the four are a VSD, an overriding aorta, infundibular RVOT obstruction and right ventricular hypertrophy.

say.text: Same stem. Which is NOT one of the four classic components of TOF?
The four are a large, anteriorly malaligned VSD, an overriding aorta, infundibular RVOT obstruction and right ventricular hypertrophy.
The answer was ASD: it is among the anomalies that may accompany TOF, but is not one of the four.
Right. ASD and PDA may accompany TOF, but the four listed by StatPearls and CDC include no ASD, PDA or LVH.
PYQs have keyed PDA, ASD and LVH as 'not part of TOF'.

sure_note.text: Good, and being sure was justified. The four are a VSD, an overriding aorta, RVOT obstruction and right ventricular hypertrophy.

say.text: You can now name the disease and spot an outsider. Can you build the whole four-part set without a list to lean on?
Next, one more stem on the set, then one on how a baby shows it.
A student writes the four components of classic TOF on the board. Which list is correct?

choices.label: VSD, overriding aorta, RVOT obstruction, left ventricular hypertrophy
VSD, overriding aorta, RVOT obstruction, right ventricular hypertrophy
VSD, ASD, RVOT obstruction, right ventricular hypertrophy

say.text: Correct. Classic TOF has a large, anteriorly malaligned VSD, an overriding aorta, infundibular RVOT obstruction and right ventricular hypertrophy.
LVH is tempting because 'ventricular hypertrophy' sounds like a general finding. But the fourth component is right ventricular hypertrophy.
The four listed by StatPearls and CDC include no ASD, PDA or LVH.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so this is the one to keep: PYQs key LVH as not part of TOF.

say.text: ASD is tempting because it often travels with TOF. But it is not one of the four, and the overriding aorta is.
The four are the VSD, overriding aorta, infundibular RVOT obstruction and right ventricular hypertrophy.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so this is the one to keep: PYQs key ASD as not part of TOF.

say.text: Back to clinic. Think of all the babies with TOF you will meet.
How does TOF most commonly present?

choices.label: As an acyanotic child found through a murmur
As cyanosis that first appears in late childhood

say.text: Yes. TOF most commonly presents as a cyanotic neonate.
It is both the most common cyanotic congenital heart disease and usually a blue-baby presentation.
This is tempting because some TOF children are barely blue: if RVOT resistance is below systemic vascular resistance, the patient is minimally cyanotic or acyanotic.
But the usual picture is a cyanotic neonate.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so note the word 'most commonly': the minimally cyanotic child is the exception.

say.text: Being the most common cyanotic lesion does not make cyanosis come late, so this is easy to blur. But TOF most commonly presents as a cyanotic neonate.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so this is the one to keep: common among cyanotic lesions, and usually blue from the neonatal period.

say.text: Next we rebuild the four from a single septum, so the set follows from logic and not from a list.
